Chapter 3: Living in Awe — Reverence for God’s Holiness and Majesty
You know, there’s a big difference between simply knowing about something and being truly awestruck by it. I mean, lots of us have heard stories about incredible beauty or greatness—but it’s a whole other thing to actually stand at the edge of the ocean, or look up at a sky full of stars. The Valley of Vision invites us to feel that kind of awe—not just at the wonders of nature, but at the holiness and majesty of God Himself.
Picture someone who’s just going through the motions, caught up in daily routines and endless distractions. Then, one night, they step outside and look up. Suddenly, the sheer vastness of the sky and the stillness of the night stir something deep inside. For a moment, all those worries and to-do lists fade away, replaced by a sense of wonder and quiet awe.
That’s the kind of reverence these prayers are meant to spark—a posture that lifts our eyes beyond ourselves.
These prayers use language that expands your heart, helping you see God as both close and unimaginably vast. He’s intimate, yet infinite. There’s this sense of trembling joy—a realization that we’re addressing a living presence who is holy and pure, not some distant force. And when that sinks in, everything changes.
Suddenly, humility doesn’t feel like a burden—it’s actually freeing. You realize just how small you are, but also how deeply you’re loved.
Reverence isn’t about fear in the sense of being terrified. It’s about deep respect and honor. Think of it like this: there’s a world of difference between treating something as ordinary, and seeing its real worth. These prayers remind us that God shouldn’t be approached casually or carelessly. His presence has a weight, a glory, that deserves our full attention.
But here’s the beautiful part—this awe doesn’t push us away. It actually draws us closer.
Let’s be honest: the busyness of life can dull our sense of wonder. The prayers in The Valley of Vision are an antidote to that. They slow us down, inviting us to pause, reflect, and remember what’s truly sacred. In a world that often treats holy things as just another part of the routine, these prayers help restore our sense of the divine. They gently remind us that we were made for more than just getting by—we were made for worship.
And this kind of reverence? It shapes not only the way we pray, but the way we live every day. It changes how we see the simple things—a meal shared, the glow of a sunrise, a heartfelt conversation with a friend. Each of these moments becomes a chance to notice God’s fingerprints, to recognize beauty and goodness that point to something beyond themselves.
So, as you move through your day, let these prayers encourage you to look at the world with fresh eyes. Notice the wonder, the holiness, and the quiet majesty all around you. Because when we live in awe, even the ordinary can become extraordinary.
